units.sentence: The PSC holds a hearing on how business customers' real-time payments count toward fuel costs; to ask wheth...
units.evidence_span: November 12, 2026 Beginning after the regularly scheduled Committee Meetings, the Commission will hear applications to intervene
units.problem: Facts are supported, but this "Act now" item gives no time (P-023 lists the hearing at 9:35 a.m., after committee meetings that start at 9:30 a.m.), no place and no phone number. The "Observe" label also implies the public may attend, which no cited passage states for this hearing (P-032 covers administrative sessions; P-025 and P-159 imply public witnesses at hearings).
units.suggested_fix: Add "after the 9:30 a.m. committee meetings (listed at 9:35 a.m.)" and the PSC phone number from P-163 (404-656-4501, press 2).

units.sentence: Submit any public comment to the PSC by this time, 24 hours before the Dec 15 session where it is scheduled...
units.marker: {computed: comments must be submitted 24 hours before a vote (P-030); the final decision is scheduled for the Dec 15 Administrative Sessi...
units.problem: Reason (valid): The arithmetic checks: the decision is set for the Dec 15 Administrative Session (P-013), which starts at 9:30 am (P-024), and 24 hours earlier (P-030) is 9:30 a.m. Dec 14. Using the session start is the earliest possible deadline, so the stated time is safe.

units.sentence: The PSC's Energy Committee takes up the case at its meeting, which begins at 9:30 a.m.
units.evidence_span: This matter shall be considered at the scheduled Energy Committee Meeting, which begins at 9:30 a.m.

units.sentence: The PSC is scheduled to decide how much of business customers' real-time payments counts toward fuel costs.
units.evidence_span: A Final Decision on this proceeding will be made by the Commission on December 15, 2026 at the regularly scheduled Administrative Session.

units.sentence: Georgia Power filed the last written testimony.
units.evidence_span: October 27, 2026 Georgia Power may file any pre-filed rebuttal testimony in Docket 57171 by 4:00 p.m.

units.sentence: It and an interfaith group want solar, wind and biomass contracts taken out of the fuel credit entirely, wh...
units.evidence_span: The Company and GIPL recommend the Commission approve Option 1.
units.problem: Minor scope: the options cover all take-or-pay (non-dispatchable) contracts, which P-063 says also include Qualifying Facilities. "Taken out of the fuel credit" means taken out of the credit's calculation. Georgia Power offered both options and prefers Option 1 (P-065). The item says the credit grows but not that the same dollars come off the base side (P-061, P-115).

framing_issues.issue: An "Act now" item with no start time (P-023: 9:35 a.m., after the 9:30 a.m. committee meetings), no place and no phone number, though it tells readers to call. "Observe" implies the public may attend, which the cited passages don't state for this hearing.

framing_issues.text: Submit any public comment to the PSC by this time
framing_issues.issue: Tells readers to submit a comment but gives no way to do it. The PSC page (P-030) gives none, so the item should point to the PSC contacts (P-163). There is also no "dates can change" caveat on a computed deadline.

Says only that the credit grows, which sounds like a plain benefit to customers. It leaves out that the same dollars come off the base side and base rates could rise later (P-061, P-115, P-105). GAM's view is also absent.
Georgia Power and PIA Staff are named by role, but GIPL is described only as "an interfaith group." Use its name or role, as the workspace does.
